history.summary: The Hanuman Mandir at Ramna Maidan (also listed as Ramna Hanuman Mandir), near the Old Police Line on East Ramna Road, is a well-known modern Hanuman temple in Arrah town (rated ~4.9 on listings). No published founding history or builder was found; it appears to be a contemporary community temple. No non-Hindu flag.

name: Hanuman Mandir, Arrah
town_description: Arrah (also spelled Ara) is the administrative headquarters of Bhojpur district in Bihar, situated on the banks of the Son River about 60 km west of Patna. An ancient town with a history going back to the Dvapara Yuga legends and the 1857 rebellion (home of Veer Kunwar Singh), it is known for the Aranya Devi temple, Ramna Maidan, the 18th-century Kila Arrah and the Mughal-era Shahi Masjid. It is well connected by rail (Arrah Junction) and road via NH 30.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna (~60 km east); taxi/bus onward
travel.railway: Arrah Junction, ~2-3 km from Ramna Maidan
travel.road: Ramna Maidan / East Ramna Road, central Arrah; auto-rickshaws and e-rickshaws throughout town

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Tuesdays and Hanuman Jayanti are busiest
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily roughly 5:00 AM-9:00 PM, extended on Tuesdays (sources conflict slightly: one listing shows Tue 4:00 AM-10:00 PM and Fri 4:00 AM-10:00 PM; verify)
